architecture: A1 — Size-Selective Filtration Membrane Integrated into eShunt Lumen
recommended_material: PTFE expanded membrane (ePTFE) — established vascular implant precedent, tunable pore size, proven chronic biocompatibility
pore_size_regime: VALIDATION_REQUIRED — must retain therapeutic agent (scAAV9 ~25nm diameter) while passing CSF fluid and small molecules. Estimated: 50-200 nm pore size.
lumen_integration: Membrane integrated as a circumferential liner within the eShunt lumen, positioned distal to the one-way valve. CSF flows through the membrane into the venous system. Therapeutic agent (if >pore size) is retained in the subarachnoid space.
flow_path: Subarachnoid space → eShunt proximal opening → membrane-lined lumen → one-way valve → dural venous sinus
pressure_drop_constraints: VALIDATION_REQUIRED — membrane must not create clinically significant pressure drop. eShunt operates at 3-5 mm Hg differential. Membrane resistance must be <1 mm Hg at target flow (5-15 mL/hr).

therapeutic_agent_characteristics.gene_therapy_vectors: scAAV9 ~25 nm — retainable with 50 nm pore
therapeutic_agent_characteristics.small_molecules: <1 nm — NOT retainable by size alone (would need affinity mechanism)

deployment_constraints: Must fit through eShunt delivery catheter (sub-millimeter). Membrane must be self-expanding or pre-formed.
chronic_implantation_constraints: Permanent implant in dural venous sinus. Must withstand venous pulsation, blood contact on distal side, CSF contact on proximal side.
failure_modes: Membrane fouling → increased resistance → reduced drainage → ICP elevation
Membrane rupture → loss of retention (drug drains — no ICP risk)
manufacturing_pathway: Membrane fabrication (extrusion/stretching for ePTFE) → lumen integration (adhesive or thermal bonding) → sterilization (EtO or gamma) → delivery catheter loading
alternative_embodiments: Annular membrane ring (not full lumen liner)
